FX-EDGES-001.says: Gaussian Blur, sigma 1, edges repeat, on a picture that fills the layer: every pixel stays fully covered, the edges as solid as the middle, and the middle is blurred exactly as without it.

FX-EDGES-002.says: Gaussian Blur, sigma 1, edges written "transparent": the rule as it always was, the edges fading, the same as a file without the setting.

FX-EDGES-003.says: FX-EDGES-001 moved three pixels right: the layer does not grow, so the three columns left of it stay empty.

FX-EDGES-004.says: Directional Blur, direction 90, length 6, edges repeat, on the picture: streaked left and right, every pixel still fully covered.

FX-EDGES-005.says: Directional Blur, direction 30, length 8, edges repeat: a slanting streak whose samples leave the layer across both edges, every pixel still fully covered.

FX-EDGES-006.says: Directional Blur, direction 90, length 6, edges repeat, on the bars moved three pixels right: the line on the drawing's left edge carries on past it, so its column keeps more of the line than FX-DIRBLUR-009's, and nothing is drawn left of the drawing.

FX-EDGES-007.says: Radial Blur, spin 30 about the middle, edges repeat, on the picture: every pixel still fully covered, the corners too.

FX-EDGES-008.says: Radial Blur, zoom 40 about the top left corner, edges repeat: every pixel still fully covered.

FX-EDGES-009.says: A Directional Blur, direction 90 and length 4, edges transparent, then FX-EDGES-007's spin: the spin repeats the edge of its own input, the layer the Directional Blur grew two pixels on every side, whose outer columns have faded.

FX-EDGES-010.says: Gaussian Blur with edges "wrap", which is not a way of treating edges. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-EDGES-011.says: Directional Blur with edges "Repeat": the word is exact, so a capital is not it. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-EDGES-012.says: Radial Blur with edges "", empty. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.
